notes.title: About Difficulty in Limerick: Cadence Mansion
notes.content:
Difficulty in games varies wildly from player to player. Games that seem too easy to some will be challenging for others, and vice versa. Limerick: Cadence Mansion is no exception to this. Balancing difficulty is something I am continuing to work on.

Here's a brief breakdown of where I'm at with difficulty in Limerick and what my philosophy has been and will be moving forward.


[h2]SCALABILITY[/h2]

If you've missed it, I've added quite a few scalability options for difficulty in Limerick. Unlike most games, these options do not affect combat/weapons/etc. Instead, they focus on scaling what people are finding [i]truly[/i] difficult in Limerick: puzzles and encounters with the marionette himself.

This will continue to be my focus moving forward. I am staying true to my design philosophy as I craft new areas and experiences. But after this I return and explore avenues on how I can help players bypass some of the greater challenges. This even includes the addition of some new mechanics (most recently, exploding barrels) that give players a wider arsenal of tools to manage Limerick and his minions.


[h2]PAIN & FAIRNESS[/h2]

So, what motivated me to make the game so challenging to begin with? The short answer is that I like challenging games. It is only natural that I pursued ways to create that kind of challenge in my own game.

But there is a deeper, lore-driven aspect to this design choice. Limerick is [i]supposed[/i] to be incredibly powerful. He is supposed to be able to subvert, frustrate, and ultimately decimate his opponents. Of course, I want you to overcome and triumph over your wily opponent. But part of my design philosophy has been to induce a level of pain, frustration, and anger in your failed attempts to defeat Limerick. To me, that makes the thrill of triumphing over his cheeky little face [i]all the more rewarding[/i] when you finally accomplish it!

But in order for any of that to work, the encounters with Limerick must be [i]fair[/i], even if they are also [i]unforgiving[/i]. This is the area where I am putting my greatest focus. Having Limerick spawn directly behind you and one-shot you does not feel [i]fair[/i]. Getting stuck on an enemy collision capsule does not feel [i]fair[/i]. Getting held up by a glitch, bug, or misplaced object does not feel [i]fair[/i]. These are the issues I am prioritizing and will continue to work on hardest.

I also know that challenge driven games like Limerick are not for everyone. While I do believe that the aforementioned scalability can greatly help widen the audience, I have also realized that I have to be true to the design of the game. Limerick: Cadence Mansion is [i]driven[/i] by puzzles, resource management, and multi-layered survival mechanics. It is meant to reward you for the proper use of its systems. It is meant to be loaded with deep and intricate lore, a bevy of personal stories, and loads of monsters that can and will kill you when given the opportunity.


[h2]A NOTE ON TEDIUM[/h2]

Another thing I want to try and avoid is the game just feeling downright tedious. Unfortunately, this is another area in which opinions vary [i]wildly[/i]. The Limerick encounters themselves serve as an excellent example of this. Some players - while enjoying the puzzles as a whole - strongly disliked having to solve puzzles three times in a row while dealing with the presence of Limerick. They found it painful, tedious, and boring.

Others - including myself - thoroughly enjoy this challenge. Armed with the knowledge of how to solve the puzzles, players thrust themselves into the larger game of completing these cycles while being pursued by their opponent. They find the thrill not in the puzzles, but in the challenge of staying alive while racing through the halls of Limerick's arenas.

How do I bring these two disparate views into harmony? Believe me when I say that I am trying my best! I will continue to explore scalability settings, and some of the new options can greatly reduce the feeling of tedium for some players by bypassing some of these puzzle cycles.



Thank you all so much for your continued support and for taking time to play the demo. The witty, wonderful, whimsical world of Limerick continues to come together, and I cannot wait to share the final product soon!

notes.title: About the Game Menu
notes.content:
Thankfully, most players seem to be able to navigate the options menu for Limerick: Cadence Mansion without too much of a problem.

However, I know some of you have found it bulky and frustrating. I wanted to "pull back the curtain" and give you an honest post about why it works the way it does and what I [i]might[/i] be able to do in the future.


[h2]ORIGINAL DEVELOPMENT[/h2]

I developed the menu a while back. At that time, I had great difficulty getting UE's built-in menu tools to work with [i]both[/i] mouse/keys & gamepad. I want you to be able to play the WHOLE game with either input. To me, there is nothing more frustrating than being told I can use a gamepad just to have to set it down 3 seconds later to navigate a menu. 

Eventually, I built my own solution for the menu. But I did not build extra options like sliders, radio buttons, etc. This is why the menu can be so bulky at times. On the positive side, you can navigate all settings with either input!


[h2]CURRENT PRIORITY[/h2]

As a solo developer, my current priority is 100% on [i]finishing the game[/i]. I think everyone can understand this. The flashiest menu on earth will never make up for a game that is not finished or absolutely riddled with bugs.

I'm glad to be on-track with development. Cadence Mansion is coming together nicely, and it shouldn't be too long before some very, very, VERY big announcements will roll along.


[h2]LOOKING AHEAD[/h2]

Until I've finished primary development (i.e. getting the game done), the menu is not a priority issue for me. While a bit bulky, it serves its purpose faithfully and can be used with any input method the player has chosen.

Once the game is done - and probably already launched - I [i]may[/i] be able to come back around to the menu and see what I can do to spruce it up.


Thank you all so much for playing and for the continued feedback!

notes.title: Steam Next, New Demo, and Feedback Response
notes.content:
Hello everyone! Let me start by saying - again - THANK YOU ALL. I have received so much support and encouragement with the development of Limerick: Cadence Mansion, and I am extremely excited to share this new demo with the world.

I want to provide a few key pieces of information as Steam Next kicks off.


[h2]ABOUT THE DEVELOPER[/h2]
I want to be upfront with everyone that I am a [b]solo dev[/b], as in I quite literally do basically everything by myself. The only exception to this is the lovely voice acting provided by Andy Mack and the use of a few (emphasis on [i]few[/i]) asset packs.

I don't want this to be an excuse, but I would ask that you understand I do not have a team, I do not have a massive budget, and I do not have a big publisher behind me (Jenito Studios, LLC is just me, too). While this allows me to be more personal than a large developer, it also means that there are some things I cannot realistically accomplish right now.


[h2]DEMO LENGTH, SCOPE & DIFFICULTY[/h2]
The demo generally runs about an hour and a half for a lot of people, but it will vary wildly from player to player. There are also difficulty options that can help you get through much quicker if you are pressed for time. I know - there are a [i]lot[/i] of games to try this week!

This demo focuses on introducing you to the mechanics of the game, allowing you to enjoy some exploration and experience an encounter with Limerick the marionette.

It is important to know that Limerick is not designed to be a particularly easy game. It offers a wide array of challenges, and I think it shines best when you must fight to survive. However, I have added multiple settings that can make the experience [i]much[/i] more forgiving, and I strongly encourage you to use them if the game is being unenjoyable for you.

Let me also say up front that if you enjoy the demo, I think you will definitely enjoy the complete game. If you don't enjoy the demo, I want to be transparent: it is unlikely that all that much about the current experience is going to change between now and release. While I will be taking and implementing some feedback, the core experience is unlikely to be much different.


[h2]ABOUT FEEDBACK[/h2]
I have recently experienced a massive spike in new feedback. I am VERY happy about that and extremely thankful!

As a solo dev, you can imagine that my time is severely limited. I want you to know that I look at [i]all[/i] the feedback I get, and I will continue to do so. I always prioritize fixing things that are causing consistent problems for a large portion of players.

However, I highly doubt I will be able to answer every question or respond to every suggestion individually. Please look to larger announcement posts for more generalized reactions to feedback, along with updates on what steps I am taking.

I want to make the game as widely playable as possible. I know the end product will not be for everyone, but I want to do what I can to help players enjoy Limerick: Cadence Mansion.


Thank you all so much for your continued support! I look forward to everyone exploring the wonderful world of Limerick this week.

notes.title: Demo Patch #3, Version 0.4.4.73
notes.content:
This patch is mostly focused on tutorial and QOL improvements along with one small bug fix.

[h1]PATCH NOTES[/h1]
[list]
[*]No longer able to collide with and get hung up on health pickups

[*]Added a map players can examine before entering the Circus of Hammers

[*]Added a sign that indicates the power meter on chargers during the tutorial

[*]Added a sign to guide players towards the rest of the tutorial after learning Panic Closets

[*]Added volumes that check if the player is still crouching during the tutorial or before entering the map and advise them to stand back up

[*]Increased light emitted by dolls

[*]Increased light emitted by health pickups

[*]Adjusted 2 doll spawn points to increase visibility
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Patch #1, Version 0.4.4.71
notes.content:
The first patch for the Limerick Demo has arrived with a load of small changes that will better balance difficulty, improve the experience, and welcome new players. I've highlighted these changes below.

[h1]PATCH NOTES[/h1]
[list]
[*]Greatly reduced difficulty of Mere Essayist

[*]Greatly increased the difficulty of Master of Writ

[*]Changed the number of dolls you must collect based on difficulty: 8 on Mere Essayist; 15 on I, Proofreader; 21 on Master of Writ

[*]Changed the rate of Elegy spawning based on difficulty

[*]Changed the amount of time you have to find a doll based on difficulty: 9 minutes on Mere Essayist; 6 minutes on I, Proofreader; 4 minutes on Master of Writ

[*]Added health pickups

[*]Added resource pickups

[*]Decreased/removed pickups based on difficulty

[*]It is no longer possible to run out of Essence (flashlight) before being prompted to use it in the tutorial section (or before entering the map if you skip the tutorial)

[*]Improved tutorial reflects changes to amount of dolls needed to win

[*]Decreased the volume of the player breathing noise

[*]Increased the volume emitted by dolls

[*]Increased doll brightness and intensity

[*]Increased range of the "Wheel of Death" sound

[*]Slightly increased the volume of the "Wheel of Death" sound
[/list]

notes.title: Demo 0.4.4.7 Released!
notes.content:
[h2]ABOUT THE DEMO[/h2]

I'm very excited to announce that the first playable demo of Limerick: Cadence Mansion releases today! Here's a breakdown of what you need to know:

[list]
[*]This demo [i]does not[/i] include any of the story

[*]The complete game will have several "sandbox modes" where you can jump straight into an encounter with Limerick - this demo is one such mode

[*]This is the first public release and therefore prone to have some bugs

[*]Limerick is a systems-driven horror experience, so you should be prepared to die a lot at first as you learn the different techniques for surviving and triumphing

[*]Limerick really wants to say hello, so get downloading!
[/list]

[h2]KNOWN GRAPHICS ISSUE[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43134231/2fd91a21d1d7cf29c3d51a6563737bb472eb496c.png[/img]

On certain graphics card, the pictured artifacts can occur after making changes to the graphics settings. These anomalies are directly related to real-time global illumination. I've done everything I can to try and mitigate this as much as possible, but (based on my testing so far) there are some quick and easy solutions to get the artifacts to disappear.

[olist]
[*]Make sure to update your graphics drivers to the latest version

[*]After adjusting your graphics settings, [b]close and restart the game[/b] (so far this eliminates the problem entirely unless you adjust your graphics settings again, at which point you would need to again close and restart)

[*]If all else fails, disable global illumination in the advanced graphics settings (you will still get a good visual experience even without global illumination)
[/olist]

[h2]BUG REPORTING[/h2]

If you encounter a bug, please report it via Jenito's Twitter account or e-mail me directly through the Jenito contact page.

[url=https://twitter.com/Jenito_studios]Jenito Studios on Twitter[/url]

[url=https://www.jenito.com/contact]Jenito Studios' Contact Page[/url]

Thank you for playing!
